problem: The helix-cli is the tool surface that the proposed host-agent-proxy MCP pattern would use to fulfill requests. If the MCP becomes a thin message-passing layer to a host agent, that agent relies entirely on the CLI's capabilities. The CLI's current command surface, skill system, and authentication model define the boundaries of what the host-agent MCP could offer.

files.why: CLI entry point — command router dispatching to all major subsystems. Defines the full surface of hlx commands available to the host agent.
Agent-consumable skill documentation — describes the CLI's capabilities as seen by AI agents. The host agent would rely on this surface.
Skill installation system — installs CLI as a skill to Claude Code and Codex agents. Shows the current agent integration pattern.
Ticket creation command — currently on the host agent's CLI deny list. Illustrates command-level access control boundaries.
Database inspection command — demonstrates read-only production access through the CLI.
Log inspection command — another read-only production tool available via CLI.
Comment posting — currently on the host agent's CLI deny list for safety.
Library report access — demonstrates CLI read capabilities the host agent can use.
Configuration and auth — multi-org support, env var fallback (HELIX_API_KEY, HELIX_URL). Host agent authenticates via these.
HTTP client with retry logic — 3 attempts, exponential backoff, 30s timeout. Defines reliability characteristics for CLI-via-host-agent.
Comprehensive CLI documentation compiled into TypeScript — exported as @projectxinnovation/helix-cli/docs.
Binary: hlx (dist/index.js). Exports: docs, skill-content/SKILL.md. Build: tsc. Test: tsc && node --test.

facts: CLI binary is 'hlx' with entry point dist/index.js, published as @projectxinnovation/helix-cli on npm
Major command groups: login, token, org, tickets (11 subcommands), goals (6 subcommands), inspect (repos/db/logs/api), comments (list/post), library (list/show/comments), skill (show/install), update
Skill system installs CLI documentation to ~/.claude/skills/hlx-cli/ or ~/.codex/skills/hlx-cli/ for agent consumption
Host agent's CLI deny list blocks: 'tickets create', 'comments post', 'tickets continue', 'tickets rerun', 'tickets archive' — these are safety-critical write operations
Authentication supports multi-org contexts with HELIX_API_KEY/HELIX_URL env vars or stored config via hlx login
HTTP client has retry logic with exponential backoff (3 attempts, retryable: 429, 500, 502, 503, 504) and 30s timeout
The CLI is installed globally on host agent sprites via 'npm install -g @projectxinnovation/helix-cli'
Host agent authenticates CLI via inspection API key written to /app/.helix-env on the sprite
unknowns: Whether the CLI's current command surface is sufficient for all use cases currently covered by the 13 MCP tool modules — some MCP tools may expose operations not available via the CLI
Whether the host agent CLI deny list would need revision if the MCP were fully proxied through the host agent — the deny list was designed for ticket-scoped use, not organization-wide access
Whether file upload/download operations (currently handled by MCP attachments tool) have a CLI equivalent for host-agent proxying
Whether the CLI needs new commands to support capabilities that the current MCP tools provide but the CLI does not (e.g., sprint management, staging queue, deployment triggers)
